speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This Plan is for officers in the uniformed services under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These officers have an earlier retirement age of 55.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They receive additional contributions under the INVEST Plan, on top of full Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions, to help them with their career transition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These additional contributions under the INVEST Plan are pooled to form an investment fund known as the INVEST Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Fund invests in a diversified portfolio, managed by a Board of Trustees appointed by the Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Board comprises senior members from the Home Team and members with relevant experience from the finance industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MHA has reviewed best practices in the investment management industry to achieve the Fund’s objectives of achieving appropriate risk-adjusted long-term returns and improving the management of the Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill proposes to make the necessary legislative amendments to align with industry best practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The key provisions relate to two main areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, the broadening of the range of permissible investments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, the Board is empowered to invest in "stocks, funds, securities and investments".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: One example is the use of derivatives to protect the value of the Fund and invest more cost-efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The use of derivatives will be guided by best practices, such as the Code on Collective Investment Schemes issued by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, the delegation of the Board’s powers and functions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This approach can help to achieve lower investment management fees through economies of scale that the investment managers would have.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The amendments for delegation are in line with industry practice for other large pension funds and are consistent with the powers of delegation found in other legislation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Board will maintain investment oversight of the Fund and will have a clear governance framework and reporting structures in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Board remains fully accountable to the Minister for the management of the Fund.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Due to the physical requirements of service, our Home Affairs Officers face an earlier retirement than Singaporeans in other professions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It is right that we reward them for their service and ensure that they are not financially disadvantaged compared to their peers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: First, I will suggest that we separate the role that the INVEST Fund plays as a retirement benefit from that of a good-performance bond.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Second, I will suggest that, based on behavioural finance, we consider shaping the investment choices made by INVEST members to improve their retirement benefits.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The INVEST Fund is essentially a deferred compensation scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They protect the employees against their own tendency to fail to set aside funds for their own future, and they serve as a good-performance bond, because the benefits only vest when employees serve faithfully over time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The public expects a high standard of behaviour from Uniformed Officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But the question is whether we should ensure this by putting up the entire value of an Officer’s INVEST account as a good-performance bond.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I would argue that the judicial system is the more appropriate means of punishing errant behaviour in Uniformed Service Officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Officers are already held to higher standards in the judicial system because of the trust reposed in them and the considerable powers they have which could be abused.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If this standard is not high enough today, Parliament may increase criminal sanctions for public servants who abuse their trust by amending the relevant laws.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In contrast, the reduction or termination of INVEST benefits for errant Officers is an administrative punishment and not a judicial one.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This would follow best practices for deferred compensation in the private sector, where a portion of benefits vest permanently in the employee over time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Nothing in this suggestion precludes the Government from recovering financial assets or penalties, as directed by the Courts, from the errant Officer's INVEST benefits.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The point is that the judicial process should take its course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The administrative penalty of reducing or terminating INVEST benefits could be revised in line with private sector practices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I will now turn to the investment choices made by Officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Traditionally, retirement fund administrators have focused on ensuring that the fund's investment strategies are as robust as possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I have reviewed the INVEST annual reports and I believe that this task has been carried out responsibly by the Board over the years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But a factor that is equally important is the role the retirement fund plays in helping members make the best investment choices possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This is not straightforward because behavioural biases, limited information, and poor financial literacy, all can contribute to poor financial decision-making.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Since 2010, Officers have been able to choose from three investment plans offered by INVEST, with progressively higher risk and return, namely, the Stable, Balanced and Dynamic Plans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The Dynamic Plan takes on the greatest risk with 70% of the funds invested in equities while the Stable Plan invests entirely in safe bonds and cash.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The Balanced Plan is 40% equities and 60% bonds and cash.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The funds are invested with reputable global investment managers and expenses are low due to economies of scale.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, because of that, the returns are driven largely by the asset allocation strategies of each of these plans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, the Stable Plan has experienced lower returns than that of the CPF Ordinary Account.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Over 10 years, that is a difference of about $600 in returns per $10,000 invested in the Stable Plan, compared to CPF.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This low return is a necessary consequence of the fact that the Stable Plan invests entirely in safe bonds and cash.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: My concern is if an Officer is not aware of these low expected returns of the Stable Plan, or is very risk-averse, they are likely to have a much lower retirement benefit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I would suggest the Ministry explore whether Officers who are very risk-averse may be allowed to transfer their INVEST funds, as they vest, to their CPF accounts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The broader point is that the Officer's retirement benefit will largely depend on their investment plan choice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If they choose the higher risk Dynamic Plan early in their career they will, on average, obtain a larger retirement benefit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: As they approach retirement age, they may wish to reduce risk by reallocating their investment to the Stable Plan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This is the standard advice given by financial planning experts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The international evidence suggests most members of retirement plans do not make active choices about their investment portfolio.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, many members make choices based on the default provided by the retirement plan administrator.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The default was a money market fund that is safe but provides very low returns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In general, the research in behavioural finance suggests that retirement plan choices are far from optimal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They are made on the basis of little financial advice or planning and can be significantly shaped by irrelevant factors ranging from peer effects to advertising, to the way the retirement fund administrator presents choices to the member.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I would suggest that the INVEST Fund structure the default investment choices in such a way as to meet the needs of the broad majority of officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I am sure that this is already done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For example, one common strategy in the private retirement fund industry is to recommend a lifecycle fund.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These funds automatically adjust the level of risk as the investor approaches payout age, so that a higher level of risk is taken early on to build assets, and a low level of risk is adopted later to secure the value of those assets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I would also suggest that the Ministry make more information about INVEST publicly available, such as details on investment strategies and performance, investment plan choices available to and made by the officers and so on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This may be attractive to potential recruits to the Home Team and will also help existing officers make more informed decisions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I do have a few questions for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singaporeans statistically have one of the longest life expectancies in the world, at 84.8 years old.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, on average, 10 of those years will be spent in poor health.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With the combination of these two trends – increased life expectancies and extended periods of ill health – it is important that we ensure that our Home Team officers, many of whom have dedicated their lives to ensure law and order in Singapore, have sufficient retirement funds to see them through their silver years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary provide an update on the review and will the age limit for officers’ contributions towards the INVEST Fund, therefore, increase in tandem with their retirement age?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition to aligning contributions to the INVEST Fund with any change to the retirement age, I would like to request the Ministry to review the mandatory closure of INVEST accounts for retired officers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With many officers opting to continue with a second career post-retirement, they may not have any immediate need to utilise their retirement funds.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry, therefore, allow such officers with the flexibility to remain invested in the Fund and enjoy the returns from their sizeable accumulation of savings?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Decoupling the closure of the INVEST account with an officer's employment in service will also allow the INVEST Fund managers to use the additional funds to grow its investments, thereby benefiting all its members.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to seek a clarification on what would happen to the INVEST Fund monies for ex-officers who have had their service terminated.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I understand that the Ministry treats such dismissals very seriously, since the INVEST Fund is principally meant to function as a retirement fund, perhaps we could afford to be more lenient towards such officers who have already been punished by having their service terminated.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And on a yearly basis, how many retired officers fail to embark on their second career six months after retirement?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Home Affairs uniformed officers are equipped with a wide variety of skillsets, have ample experience in handling difficult situations and would be valuable assets to any organisation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I believe that with the right support in place, many would go on to find a fulfilling second career.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I note that the Ministry has a five-year career transition roadmap to support retiring officers in their career transition, I would like to know if the Ministry has targeted programmes to help officers enter high growth segments, such as cybersecurity and fintech.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps the Police co-operatives would like to consider working together with the National Trades Union Congress to do more to assist retiring officers with job placements in these high growth segments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But I believe that we can further improve the retirement adequacy of our Home Affairs uniformed officers by decoupling the closure of INVEST Fund accounts with their continued employment, to provide our retired officers with an option of benefiting from a longer investment period.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We also need to provide better support to help them transit to a second career.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about the progress of the review of Home Team uniformed officers' retirement age and whether the age limit for INVEST retirement contributions would be aligned with any change to the retirement age.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As part of this review, MHA is also studying related areas, such as the age limit for INVEST retirement contributions and the INVEST vesting scale.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Melvin Yong also asked whether MHA could decouple the closure of INVEST account from officers' employment so as to give officers the flexibility to remain invested.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The INVEST plan was established to help officers transit into their second career.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As they have an earlier retirement age of 55 as compared to the rest of the Civil Service at 62 and also compared to the Civil Service's re-employment age of 67, this benefit ceases upon payment of the INVEST monies to officers at retirement.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Keeping officers invested with the INVEST Fund when they are no longer in service would not be in line with this principle.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: When INVEST monies are paid to officers, they can invest in other funds available in the market that best suit their needs at the point of retirement.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about the treatment of INVEST benefits of an officer who is dismissed from service.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked whether in such cases the officer's benefits could be protected from reduction or termination.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: First, it is important to set out that the dismissal of an officer is not taken lightly and is usually based on serious misconduct, such as fraud, corruption or other egregious conduct.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The dismissal process is a rigorous one provided for by law, such as the Public Service (Disciplinary Proceedings) Regulations and the Police Force Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It includes an inquiry to consider thoroughly, objectively and fairly the grounds for dismissal.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The superannuation scheme is a benefit awarded to officers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is over and above the market competitive salaries and the full CPF contributions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The superannuation benefits are fully funded by MHA; so, no funds are actually deducted from the officers' salary.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The superannuation benefits do not vest in the officers while they are in service.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The award of the full benefit is contingent on the officer’s satisfactory conduct and completion of the term of service.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked whether there are programmes to help officers enter high-growth job sectors, such as cybersecurity and fintech and the percentage of retired officers who found a second career within six months of retirement.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MHA’s career transition programmes are broad-based as retiring officers have diverse career interests.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The various initiatives to help retiring officers prepare for a second career include course subsidies and time-off to learn new skills to enhance employability.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MHA has also recently launched a career transition resource portal to provide officers with information on the different industries, job opportunities, career events and workshops.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MHA offers one-on-one career coaching sessions to officers to guide them on their career transition journey.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We actively engage prospective employers to source for suitable opportunities for our retiring officers and organise regular job networking sessions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We also facilitate officers' career transition by enabling them to take up a job attachment in a company prior to their retirement to try out the job.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This will help both the officer and the prospective employer to assess the fit before formal employment.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Based on our survey of our retired officers, of those who had actively looked for jobs, more than 50% were able to find new employment within six months of their retirement.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For retired officers who are looking for employment, they can continue to tap on our career transition resources.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira compared the Stable Plan returns with returns from the CPF Ordinary Account.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This is not a like-for-like comparison and, hence, it is not an appropriate comparison, as they are, in fact, separate schemes with different objectives.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In terms of returns, CPF Ordinary Account has a guaranteed floor of 2.5%, and this is a special arrangement guaranteed by the Singapore Government.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: All CPF accounts, including Special, Retirement Accounts, are subject to CPF rules on withdrawal and use of funds.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In contrast, INVEST offers several options and the returns of these options are subject to market conditions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked whether officers who have low risk appetite may be allowed to transfer their INVEST Funds as they vest to their CPF accounts.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: CPF and INVEST have different structures, rules and entitlement terms.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In the case of CPF, members can use their CPF savings in their Ordinary Accounts for housing investments and education, subject to the terms and conditions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Usage of funds is not contingent on the change in employment or specific rules set by the employer.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In contrast, the INVEST monies are paid to the officer only upon satisfaction of conditions, such as satisfactory conduct and completion of service.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Officers can choose from three INVEST plans during service.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Upon retirement, officers can top up their CPF accounts with INVEST monies subject to CPF limits and rules, or they can choose to invest in other financial products available in the market.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked the Ministry to periodically review the investment strategies and investment plan choices by officers and to structure the default investment choices in such a way as to meet the needs of the majority of the officers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Each Plan has its own risk return objectives and the Plans' performance is communicated to officers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As their circumstances change, officers can change Plan over the course of their career.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: MHA conducts reviews on investment choices as part of ongoing studies on industry best practices.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked the Ministry to make more information about INVEST publicly available as it may be attractive to potential recruits to the Home Team and to help existing officers make informed choices.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The current recruitment process informs all potential recruits about INVEST and the information is also available on the Home Team departments' websites.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Officers are kept informed on the investment plans via several platforms, such as onboarding briefings, semi-annual Statement of Accounts, e-newsletters and investment deck are published on MHA's Intranet which includes an investment choice guide and the historical performance of the plans.
